items.content:
DeepSeek Harness desktop is the biggest change in the v0.2 update: the open-source agent harness now runs as a proper app on Mac and Windows instead of a terminal plus a browser tab, and it’s completely free. I installed it the day it dropped and walked through everything in the video below — the setup, the plugin library, the new scheduled automation, and how to run it on free models so the whole thing costs nothing.

Key takeaways

- The v0.2 update turns DeepSeek Harness into a free desktop app for macOS and Windows, downloaded from deepseek.com/harness.

- Your previous sessions and projects carry over automatically.

- A built-in plugin manager, agent teams, voice input and scheduled automation tasks come included.

- Plug in free models via OpenCode or OpenRouter and the whole stack costs nothing.

## What the DeepSeek Harness desktop app is

DeepSeek Harness is an open-source agent harness — MIT licensed, 243K+ GitHub stars, built on an “everything is a plugin” architecture. Until v0.2 you ran it from the terminal and opened the web UI in a browser. The desktop app wraps the same harness in a native window, so you double-click and you’re in.

Think of it as an AI employee on your own computer: it codes, organises files, builds presentations and runs recurring jobs while you do something else. It sits in the same category as Hermes and OpenClaw, but its standout trait is how much you can customise through plugins.

- Native desktop app for macOS and Windows — no more running it in a terminal and opening a browser tab.

- Your history comes with you: my earlier sessions, projects and Obsidian vault were all there when I opened the app.

- Built-in plugin manager: web search, sub-agents, agent loops, shell, voice input and automation, switched on and off in one place.

- Bundled `dsh` command for installing plugins, managed from the menu bar — no separate Node or pnpm install.

- Automation tasks: scheduled, recurring jobs that keep running in the background even when the window is closed.

- Better file handling: documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, charts and slide decks, with previews in the sidebar.

## DeepSeek Harness desktop setup in five minutes

Here’s exactly how I set it up:

- Download the app from deepseek.com/harness — macOS (Apple Silicon) or Windows (64-bit). Full details in my download guide.

- Open it — any sessions from the web version appear automatically.

- Add a model provider in the models section. For free, pick OpenCode or OpenRouter and paste an API key.

- Start a new session, choose a project folder and a mode (I use Creator mode).

- Switch on the plugins you want — agent teams, voice input, automation — and get building.

The one step most people miss: choosing the mode. Standard works, but Creator mode is where you can build and customise plugins, which is the whole point of this harness.

The automation task plugin is the feature I’m most excited about: set a recurring job — say, every Monday build a slide deck on the week’s AI automation news — and it runs on schedule, even with the window closed. The v0.2 desktop app for DeepSeek’s open-source agent harness — a native Mac and Windows app replacing the old terminal-plus-browser setup.

From deepseek.com/harness, which offers macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (64-bit) builds.

Not as an official desktop app yet; Linux users run it with npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web or a community desktop client.

Yes — my previous sessions, projects and vault appeared automatically in the desktop app.

DeepSeek Harness desktop Linux support is the question I got most after my v0.2 video — and the straight answer is that there’s no official Linux desktop download yet. Key takeaways

- No official Linux desktop app on deepseek.com/harness yet.

- Run it anyway with `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` — the web UI opens at 127.0.0.1:3080.

- Community desktop clients built with Tauri offer.deb,.rpm and AppImage builds.

- v0.2 fixed npm install failures on some Linux systems.

## Running DeepSeek Harness on Linux the official way

The official route on Linux is the npm package:

- Install Node.js.

- Run `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.

- Open `http://127.0.0.1:3080` in your browser.

- Or clone `github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` and build from source.

You get the same harness, plugins and modes as the desktop app — just in a browser tab. The v0.2.0 release fixed npm installs failing on Linux systems missing optional native packages.

DeepSeek Harness is built on an “everything is a plugin” architecture — the model, memory, tools and even the agent loop are swappable. items.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop Tauri: The Community Clients
items.content:
DeepSeek Harness desktop Tauri searches lead to a cluster of community projects that wrap the harness in a lightweight Tauri 2 window — useful, especially on Linux, but none of them is DeepSeek’s official app. I use the official desktop app shown in the video below, so here’s what the Tauri clients are, how they work, and when one makes sense.

Key takeaways

- Tauri is a lightweight framework for desktop apps; several community DeepSeek Harness clients use Tauri 2.

- They wrap the official dsh web interface in a native window.

- Some bundle Node and dsh; others need a Harness already running.

- They’re community projects, not official DeepSeek software.

## What the DeepSeek Harness desktop Tauri clients are

Tauri builds small, native desktop apps around a web interface. The community Tauri clients for DeepSeek Harness do exactly that with the harness’s web UI: start (or connect to) the local `dsh web` backend, then show it in a native window with a dock icon, tray and window memory.

## How the main DeepSeek Harness desktop Tauri clients differ

- dsh-desktop (xingj404-lab): a Tauri v2 shell that starts the backend itself on a loopback port, restarts it if it crashes, bundles its own node and dsh, binds to 127.0.0.1 only, and ships for macOS, Windows and Linux.

- Leon00x deepseek-harness-desktop: a Linux-native Tauri 2 / WebKitGTK client that connects to a Harness you already run locally, with.deb and AppImage builds.

- Other community repos offer Tauri shells for specific platforms, such as macOS.

## Tauri client or the official app?

On Mac and Windows I’d use the official app from deepseek.com/harness — it’s maintained by DeepSeek and gets the newest features first. On Linux, where there’s no official desktop yet, a vetted Tauri client is a reasonable way to get a native window. Either way, read the code and keep it bound to localhost.

Before you start, dated 5 October 2026: DeepSeek Harness is open source (MIT) but built by a Chinese company, so I don’t put private client data or anything sensitive into it. The desktop app is labelled a preview, and features move weekly — check the release notes for the current state.

## The bottom line on DeepSeek Harness desktop Tauri

DeepSeek Harness desktop Tauri clients are community wrappers around the official web UI — light, native and handy on Linux, but unofficial. Use the official app on Mac and Windows, and vet any Tauri client before you install it.

## What I’d set up first

- A free model through OpenCode or OpenRouter, so testing costs nothing.

- Creator mode, so you can customise plugins as you go.

- One scheduled task — a weekly report or deck — to see automation working.

- Voice input, if you like talking through tasks.

## What the official DeepSeek Harness desktop app adds over Tauri clients

The community Tauri clients wrap the same web UI, so the core features match. What the official app adds is maintenance and integration: a bundled `dsh` plugin command managed from the menu bar, platform fixes shipped weekly, background tasks that keep running after you close the window, and onboarding that helps you choose how much detail to see.

Whichever client you use, the session workflow is the same:

- Start a new session and pick the project folder you want to work in.

- Choose a mode — Creator if you want to customise, Standard for normal coding.

- Confirm your model in the session header.

- Click the plus button to open extra chats and run agents in parallel.

- Rename projects and sessions so your history stays organised.

v0.2 also made the harness far better with everyday files: it can edit documents, spreadsheets and PDFs, organise information, analyse data, make charts and build slide presentations, with previews of Office files, PDFs, images and Markdown right in the sidebar. That turns it from a coding tool into a general AI worker — I’ve had it build landing pages and decks from the same session.

### Is the DeepSeek Harness desktop app free?

Yes — the app and the harness are free and open source (MIT). You pay only for the models you connect, and you can use free models through providers like OpenCode or OpenRouter.

### Is DeepSeek Harness safe for private data?

It runs locally, but it’s built by a Chinese company, so I keep private client data out of it. The desktop app is also still labelled a preview.

### Is the official DeepSeek Harness desktop built with Tauri?

The Tauri clients you’ll find are community projects; the official app is DeepSeek’s own preview build from deepseek.com/harness.

### Which Tauri client works on Linux?

dsh-desktop (xingj404-lab) and Leon00x’s client both offer Linux builds.

### Do Tauri clients need Node?

dsh-desktop bundles node and dsh; Leon00x’s client connects to a Harness you already run.

### Are they safe?

Vet the code and keep them bound to localhost.

PostgreSQL & ElasticSearch, with the data appropriately sharded and replicated across two regions.

items.content:
I bought a wifi switch from Belkin over 10 years ago, but the app got turned off.

I wanted to use the switch to automate my mosquito repellent. Unfortunately it still had my timer running from Christmas, which meant it turned off too early. It ruined my last night's sleep.

First thing in the morning I opened the app and wanted to change the timer.

The app was offline and I read online that it is discontinued. The switch is basically garbage now.

I was pissed at first, but then I gav
